state.case_summary:
A young girl presented with a blind right eye that developed spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage. Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber. As the hyphema resolved, the number of aqueous crystals increased.

Examination revealed multiple, iridescent, needle-like crystals floating freely within the aqueous of the right eye.

- Imaging studies:    Image Title: Figure A - Slitlamp photograph    Image Description: Right eye demonstrating multiple, iridescent, needle-like crystals floating freely within the aqueous        Image Title: Figure B - Right optic disc photograph    Image Description: Shows a morning glory optic disc anomaly with low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina        Additional findings after vitreous hemorrhage resolution: Visualization revealed a morning glory disc anomaly and a chronic retinal detachment
